Same family four times, so one row with a panel count of four [geometry.panel_count].

note:
Paper 79, Team 40612, a 2015 paper that builds a collision, drift and Bayesian search model for an aircraft lost over water and then applies it to AF447 and MH370. Thirty-four pages, nineteen measured regions over fourteen pages, all of them exhibits: fourteen figure rows and five table rows, no refusal and nothing unresolved. The paper prints fourteen numbered figures and nine numbered tables; every figure and five of the tables own a region.

What the exhibits are. Seven heatmap-or-contour rows carry the probability fields - the flight dynamics prior, the reverse drift prior, the surface and underwater priors and posteriors, and the four MH370 PDFs of Figure 14 - and they are one template stamped nine times over the same Indian Ocean window, differing only in peak value and spread. Three map rows carry place rather than probability: the imagined drifter trajectories of Figure 5 over bathymetry, the pasted MH370 search-area poster of Figure 12, and the Google Earth globe of Figure 13 with the authors' own autopilot cones drawn over it. Two composites carry the computation itself - the flowchart with an inset field on p14, the allocation plan with its two-rectangle inset on p22 - and Figure 3 is the paper's single scatter, the cumulative distance distribution with its fitted curve.

The finding worth carrying out of this paper is the duplication inside Figure 2. Its pasted artwork includes a heatmap inset with the caption 'Figure 9: Underwater Search Posterior PDF for Impact Location' painted under it, so Figure 9 exists twice: once inside Figure 2 on p14 and once as its own exhibit on p20. The two rows are kept separate and the duplication is declared. The flowchart in the same picture also misspells its own box twice as 'Underwater Search Porior'.

Four printed grids are missing and that is a declared gap, not an oversight. Table 2 on p10 is a fifteen-row variable list with no rules at all, Table 3 on p28 is three unruled rows, and Tables 4 and 6 print three rules each - at 383.7/404.3/453.8 pt across 226.0 pt and at 338.0/358.7/494.8 pt across 237.5 pt - with no measured region returned for either, although both carry a caption above them and Table 6 is even cited on p28. No bbox exists to anchor a row, so none was invented.

Citation is far better here than in the rest of the run: eighteen of nineteen measured exhibits are named in prose, Figure 1 four times, and leads are mostly a single page forward. The one outlier is Table 3, announced on p23 for a grid that prints on p28. Section paths needed hand work because six regions sit at the top of a page under a heading printed on the previous one, and Figures 8 and 9 are announced under 6.5.1 and 6.5.3 but print under 6.5.4.
rules: Families split two ways by kind and four ways overall: fourteen figure rows as seven heatmap-or-contour fields, three map-or-plan-view frames, two composite-panel pictures and one each of flowchart-or-schematic and scatter, plus five table-grid rows [geometry.family].

The heatmap rows are one template stamped nine times: the same lon/lat window of 171.50-173.00 E by 14.00-15.50 N, the same rainbow ramp, white graticule and right-hand colour bar, differing only in peak value and spread. None carries an axis title, a legend or any title printed inside the picture [geometry.colorbar].

Two rows hold two different kinds of picture and are therefore composites, not panels: Figure 2 is a flowchart with a heatmap inset, Figure 10 is a heatmap with a two-rectangle map inset [geometry.panel_count].

Figure 14 breaks the panel rule the other way: four fields of the SAME family in a 2x2 block, so it is one row with a panel count of four, and its panel titles are typeset outside the block with the figure caption between the rows [geometry.panel_count].

Figure 9 is printed twice. Its caption and picture are painted inside Figure 2's inset on p14 - 'Figure 9: Underwater Search Posterior PDF for Impact Location' is legible inside the p14 artwork - and again on p20 as its own numbered exhibit. Both rows stay in the census and the duplication is stated here rather than silently merged [caption.verbatim].
Caption side is inverted between the two kinds and never mixed: all fourteen figure captions print BELOW their picture, all five measured table captions print ABOVE their grid [caption.position].

Numbering is 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:' throughout, with one ragged edge: the paper's running prose uses the same form plus a full stop when it points forward ('...is plotted in Figure 3.'), so the layer prints both 'Figure 3.' as a sentence end and 'Figure 3:' as a caption [caption.numbering].

FOUR PRINTED GRIDS ARE MISSING AND THAT IS DECLARED, NOT PATCHED: Table 2 on p10 (a fifteen-row variable list with no rules at all), Table 3 on p28 (three rows, no rules), Table 4 on p28 (three rules at 383.7/404.3/453.8 pt across 226.0 pt) and Table 6 on p29 (three rules at 338.0/358.7/494.8 pt across 237.5 pt each returned no measured region, although both carry a printed caption above them and Table 6 is even cited on p28. A rule-only grid of three rules and 70-157 pt of height is outside what the measurer returns, so no bbox exists to anchor a row [place.area_frac].

Citation is unusually complete for this lane: eighteen of the nineteen measured exhibits are named in prose and only Table 2 never is. Figure 1 carries four separate pointers across pp11, 23, 24 and 26, Figures 3, 7 and 13 carry two each, Table 7 carries two [mention.count].

Leads are mostly forward by exactly one page: Table 1, Figures 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14 and Table 5 are each cited a page before they print, and only Table 3 is cited far ahead, on p23 for a grid that prints on p28 [mention.lead_pages].

Section paths follow the last heading printed above each region, and on seven rows that heading is on the previous page: Table 1 is governed by 3.2 on p7, Figure 1 by 6.1.2 on p11, Figure 2 by 6.3.2 on p13, Figures 5 and 6 by 6.4.1.3 on p16, Figure 11 by 8.1.3 on p23, Figures 8 and 9 by 6.5.4 on p19. Figures 8 and 9 are announced under 6.5.1 and 6.5.3 and print under 6.5.4 [place.section_path].

The heading index is wrong on three rows and the printed order says so. It attributes Figure 1 to 6.2 System Module and Figure 2 to the 6.4.1.1 chain, but on p12 the 6.2 heading prints at 634.9 pt while Figure 1 occupies 121.8-307.4 pt, and on p14 the 6.4, 6.4.1 and 6.4.1.1 headings print at 463.7, 495.6 and 569.0 pt while Figure 2 occupies 121.8-414.6 pt and its caption prints at 430.4 pt - both headings come BELOW the picture they are credited with. The same pass gives Figure 5 the path of 6.4.1.1. Every path here was rebuilt from the printed line tops [place.section_path].

Width almost separates the two kinds, but not quite: the five grids run 321.2 to 464.5 pt wide and the figures 251.7 to 331.2 pt, so Figure 12's 331.2 pt is wider than Table 8's 321.2 pt. What does separate them cleanly is the raster/vector kind - every figure row is a raster and every table row has a vector grid with rules - and no figure in the paper carries a single rule or fill [place.area_frac].
